items.title: Darolutamide Maintenance Trial for Pretreated Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This Phase 2 trial is recruiting patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC) who have already received hormone therapy. It tests whether continuing darolutamide after prior treatments can extend the time before cancer progresses. Previous studies showed darolutamide maintenance improved outcomes, especially in patients who responded to earlier treatments.

items.title: Abemaciclib Plus Abiraterone Phase 3 Trial in Metastatic Hormone-Sensitive Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This Phase 3 trial tests whether adding abemaciclib (a cancer drug) to standard abiraterone plus prednisone extends the time before prostate cancer worsens in men with metastatic hormone-sensitive disease. The trial is no longer recruiting but remains active. Results could show if this combination is more effective than standard treatment.

items.title: Immunotherapy Combination for Rare Genitourinary Tumors Including Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This Phase 2 study tests cabozantinib (a targeted cancer drug) combined with two immunotherapy drugs (nivolumab and ipilimumab) in patients with rare genitourinary tumors that have spread. The trial is recruiting patients with advanced disease who have few treatment options. The combination may work better than any single drug alone.

items.title: PSMA Imaging Study for Detecting Prostate Cancer Recurrence
items.summary: This Phase 2 trial examines how bicalutamide (a hormone therapy) affects PSMA expression in prostate cancer patients with low PSA levels who have had surgery. The study uses PSMA PET/CT scans to detect residual or returning cancer. Better imaging could help doctors find cancer earlier and plan better treatments.

items.title: Mevrometostat in Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer Phase 1 Trial
items.summary: This Phase 1 trial tests mevrometostat, an investigational drug, alone or combined with enzalutamide in men with castration-resistant prostate cancer who have progressed on prior treatments. The study evaluates safety and effectiveness. Part 3 is currently recruiting patients with mCRPC.

items.title: AZD2265 Phase 3 Trial Versus Standard Care in PSMA-Positive mCRPC
items.summary: This Phase 3 trial compares AZD2265 (a new PSMA-targeted treatment) to standard therapies in patients with PSMA-positive metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study measures how long patients live without cancer progression and overall survival. It is actively recruiting and could establish a new standard treatment.

items.title: Mevrometostat Plus Enzalutamide Phase 3 Trial in Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: This Phase 3 study tests whether combining the investigational drug mevrometostat with enzalutamide works better than enzalutamide alone in patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer who have not yet received certain hormone therapies. The trial is recruiting and could lead to a new treatment option.

items.title: Sipuleucel-T Vaccine Combined With Bipolar Androgen Therapy for mCRPC
items.summary: This Phase 2 trial combines Sipuleucel-T (an FDA-approved cancer vaccine) with bipolar androgen therapy in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study measures immune response to see if the combination boosts the body's ability to fight cancer. It is currently recruiting patients.

items.title: BPX-601 CAR T-Cell Therapy Phase 1 Trial for Advanced Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This Phase 1 study tests BPX-601, a CAR T-cell therapy made from the patient's own immune cells, in men with advanced prostate cancer that has returned and spread. The trial examines safety, optimal dosing, and how well the treatment destroys cancer cells. It is currently recruiting.

items.title: Mevrometostat Plus Enzalutamide Phase 3 Trial in Metastatic Castration-Sensitive Cancer
items.summary: This Phase 3 trial tests whether combining mevrometostat with enzalutamide works better than enzalutamide alone in patients with metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer who have not received prior hormone therapy or chemotherapy. The trial is recruiting and addresses earlier-stage metastatic disease.

items.title: Phase 3 Trial Adding Darolutamide After Surgery for High-Risk Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This Phase 3 trial compares adding darolutamide to standard hormone therapy versus hormone therapy alone after surgery in men with high-risk prostate cancer. The study evaluates whether the combination better eliminates cancer or prevents recurrence. The trial is no longer recruiting new participants.

items.title: XL092 Phase 2 Trial in Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This Phase 2 study evaluates XL092, an oral investigational drug, in patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. Researchers measure how well the drug works after 16 weeks of treatment, along with safety. Patients take the drug once daily at home and return for regular checkups.

items.title: Ifinatamab Deruxtecan Phase 3 Trial Versus Chemotherapy in Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: This Phase 3 trial compares ifinatamab deruxtecan (I-DXd), a new antibody-drug conjugate, to standard chemotherapy in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study measures whether patients receiving I-DXd live longer overall and live longer without cancer progression than those receiving chemotherapy.

items.title: Cabozantinib Plus Lutetium-177-PSMA-617 Phase 1 Dose-Escalation Study
items.summary: This Phase 1 study tests the combination of cabozantinib with Lutetium-177-PSMA-617 (a radioactive drug) in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The trial determines the safest dose and evaluates effectiveness. It is currently suspended.

items.title: Luxdegalutamide Plus Lutetium-177 PSMA Phase 2 Trial in mCRPC
items.summary: This Phase 2 trial evaluates the combination of luxdegalutamide (an investigational hormone therapy) plus Lutetium-177 PSMA radioligand therapy compared to radioligand therapy alone in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer patients. The study selects the best dose for future Phase 3 trials and is no longer recruiting.

items.title: HLD-0915 Phase 1/2 Trial in Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This Phase 1/2 study evaluates the safety and effectiveness of HLD-0915 in patients with metastatic prostate cancer who have progressed on prior treatments. The study is recruiting patients and will also test the drug in other prostate cancer populations.

items.title: Inflammation Pathways Drive Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer Development
items.summary: This research paper describes how chronic inflammation, especially through NFκB and IL6/STAT3 pathways, drives prostate cancer progression and treatment resistance. These inflammatory signals work with androgen receptor signaling to promote tumor survival, growth, spread, and resistance to therapy. Understanding these pathways may lead to new treatment strategies.

items.title: PSMA DNA Vaccine Enhances Immune Response Against Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This preclinical study tested a new DNA vaccine targeting PSMA (a protein overexpressed in prostate cancer) combined with PD-1 checkpoint blockade. In animal models, the vaccine prevented tumor growth and lung metastases, increased immune activation, and improved response to immunotherapy. This approach could lead to new treatment options for aggressive prostate cancer.

items.title: Fuzuloparib Plus Abiraterone Phase 1 Study in Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: This Phase 1 study evaluated fuzuloparib (a PARP inhibitor) combined with abiraterone and prednisone in patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The trial assessed safety, drug levels in the blood, and effectiveness of the combination therapy.

items.title: Patient Quality of Life With Radium-223 Plus Olaparib Treatment
items.summary: This study examined patient-reported outcomes (quality of life, symptoms) in men with castration-resistant prostate cancer and bone metastases treated with radium-223 with or without olaparib. Understanding how treatments affect daily life helps patients and doctors make informed treatment decisions.

items.title: Raf-Mek-Erk-Rsk Pathway as Treatment Target in Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This research review examines the Raf-Mek-Erk-Rsk signaling pathway in prostate cancer, explaining how it promotes cancer growth and progression. The paper discusses how this pathway works at the molecular level and potential opportunities for developing new targeted therapies.

items.title: PI3K/AKT Pathway and PTEN Loss as Treatment Targets
items.summary: This paper discusses the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway in prostate cancer, particularly in patients with PTEN gene loss. The review explains how PTEN deficiency affects cancer behavior and discusses biomarker-guided therapy approaches that could personalize treatment based on pathway activity.

items.title: Machine Learning Model Predicts Survival in Prostate Cancer Bone Metastases
items.source: The aging male : the official journal of the International Society for the Study of the Aging Male
items.summary: Researchers developed a machine learning model to predict overall survival in prostate cancer patients with bone metastases who did not have surgery. The model identified Gleason score as the most important predictor, more important than cancer stage. This tool could help doctors assess prognosis and plan aggressive treatment for high-risk patients.

items.title: Meta-Analysis of Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors in Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: This meta-analysis of 21 clinical trials involving 1,580 patients examined immune checkpoint inhibitors in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. Combination therapy with checkpoint inhibitors showed better survival and progression-free survival than single or dual checkpoint therapy. Results suggest potential benefits but remain preliminary.
